table_title: List asteroids (including the dwarf planet Ceres, Jupiter trojans, and centaurs per Wikipedia's `List of exceptional asteroids` scope definition; excluding trans-Neptunian objects per the same scope) whose Wikipedia-cited geometric mean diameter central value is at least 250 km, with that diameter, discovery year, and discoverer. 15 rows ranked by geometric mean diameter (largest first); tiebreaker at the 254 km equality is minor-planet-number ASC.
db_analog: SELECT a.asteroid_designation AS asteroid, a.geometric_mean_diameter_km, a.discovery_year, a.discoverer FROM exceptional_asteroids a WHERE a.geometric_mean_diameter_km >= 250 ORDER BY a.geometric_mean_diameter_km DESC, a.minor_planet_number ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `List of exceptional asteroids` master article (roles = [universe, ranking, value]: scope-defines the asteroid universe, supplies the geometric-mean-diameter ranking, supplies Asteroid Number+Name / Geometric Mean Diameter (km) / Discovery Year / Discoverer cell values from the 'Largest by diameter' table; Asteroid / Diameter central value / Discoverer cells are verbatim, Discovery Year is the integer-year mechanical extraction of the source's full 'Date discovered' field), accessed 2026-05-17. source_count = 1 registered. Per-asteroid Wikipedia articles (Ceres, Vesta, Pallas, etc.) are validation-only context and NOT registered per the artifact contract. Universe = 15 rows whose Wikipedia-cited geometric mean diameter CENTRAL VALUE is at least 250 km per the master table (NOT 'unambiguously above 250 km across uncertainty bands' — Hektor 256±12 and Camilla 254±12 have lower bounds below 250; Patientia 254±3 has lower bound 251 km which does NOT dip below 250; the threshold rule is defined on the central value alone). temporal_sensitivity = low because diameter measurements are stable on benchmark timescales; minor revisions occur as new photometric / occultation data emerge but the staged 15-row set is stable. Per-row Asteroid (Number+Name) + Geometric Mean Diameter (km central value) + Discoverer cells are verbatim from the master table; Discovery Year is a mechanical integer-year extraction of the master table's full 'Date discovered' field. The ± uncertainty bands accompanying the master's Geometric Mean Diameter column are documented in normalization_decisions but stripped from the numeric staged cell (central value only). The '≥250 km central-value threshold' rule is deterministic; no curator-judgment selection.
_extraction_notes: Comparative instance — single-table threshold filter (Geometric Mean Diameter ≥ 250 km) over a closed asteroid universe defined by Wikipedia's `List of exceptional asteroids` scope clause. Brings `comparative` from gap 3 (2 of 5: countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists + tennis_players_with_more_than_5_grand_slam_singles_titles) to **gap 2 (3 of 5)**. Science/Astronomy EXISTING subdomain — Science family extends from 14 to 15 instances; Science/Astronomy subdomain extends from 3 (planets_named_moons + apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews + three_brightest_stars_in_each_zodiac_constellation) to 4 instances. NEW `taxonomic-entities/asteroids` fine-class extending under-represented taxonomic-entities bucket from 4 to 5 instances (joining moons, species, nutrients, stars — the bucket just-extended in the prior cycle by zodiac-stars). Schema: 4 cols (Asteroid PK + Geometric Mean Diameter (km) + Discovery Year + Discoverer); Geometric Mean Diameter is the ranking attribute that defines row selection (same precedent as Atomic Number in periodic-table-groups, Apparent Magnitude in zodiac-stars). Sort: Geometric Mean Diameter DESC primary (largest first), minor-planet-number ASC secondary tiebreaker at the 3-way tie at 254 km (Juno=3, Camilla=107, Patientia=451). The tiebreaker order is a curator sort normalization — the master table's native order at the 254 km tie is Juno → Patientia → Camilla, but the staged order uses minor-planet-number ASC for deterministic auditability (documented in normalization_decisions). Universe: 15 rows. claim_type = `source_defined` per audit-cycle-1 design review — universe scope clause + ranking rule + value cells all from one master table; no curator judgment after the threshold + scope-clause anchors. Audit-cycle-1 amendments applied: (1) threshold rule explicitly defined on the master table's central geometric-mean value (NOT 'unambiguously above 250 km across uncertainty bands' which was the cycle-0 false-certainty wording — Hektor 256±12 and Camilla 254±12 have lower bounds below 250); (2) exact row count documented for the alternative ≥300 km threshold = 6 rows (Ceres, Vesta, Pallas, Hygiea, Interamnia, Europa) which fails the ≥10 row gate; (3) Ceres inclusion made explicit in the title via 'including the dwarf planet Ceres per Wikipedia's `List of exceptional asteroids` scope definition' — readers expecting strict post-IAU asteroid-vs-dwarf-planet usage are pre-warned in the title; (4) Optional refinement applied: column renamed from 'Mean Diameter (km)' to 'Geometric Mean Diameter (km)' — this is a NORMALIZED label inspired by the master table's full header 'Diameter (km) (geometric mean)' (not a verbatim match to that source header) — reduces interpretation drift for irregular bodies whose diameter is a geometric-mean approximation of a triaxial ellipsoid. Entity class: `taxonomic-entities/asteroids` (NEW fine-class — asteroids are naturally-occurring celestial bodies classified by physical attributes, same bucket as moons + species + nutrients + stars).
